description: Experience the beloved flavors of Middle Eastern Lamb Ouzi with this quicker preparation, perfect for a weeknight feast. Tender lamb pieces are infused with aromatic spices and served over fragrant rice, garnished with toasted nuts. This recipe captures the essence of the traditional dish in a more accessible timeframe.

ingredients.item: Lamb shoulder or leg, boneless, cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.notes: (blend of cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, allspice, black pepper)

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of oil or ghee over medium-high heat. Add the lamb cubes and sear them on all sides until browned. Remove the lamb and set aside. This quick browning adds depth of flavor.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee to the pot. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Return the seared lamb to the pot. Add the Ouzi spice blend, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to coat the lamb evenly with the spices. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing the spices to bloom and release their aromas.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice and Lamb
instructions.text: Add the rinsed and soaked basmati rice to the pot, stirring gently to combine with the lamb and spices. Pour in the lamb broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Peas and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: After 15 minutes, stir in the frozen peas. Re-cover the pot and continue to cook on low heat for another 5 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. If using pre-cooked lamb, ensure it is heated through.

instructions.title: Rest and Garnish
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld and the rice to become fluffy. Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Transfer the Lamb Ouzi to a large serving platter, garnish generously with toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, toast the Ouzi spice blend lightly in a dry pan before adding it to the lamb.
If you prefer a richer taste, use ghee instead of vegetable oil for cooking the lamb and rice.
To achieve perfectly fluffy rice, avoid lifting the lid during the cooking process and allow it to rest undisturbed after cooking.
article:
Unveiling a true jewel of Middle Eastern cuisine, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is more than just a meal; it's a celebration, a testament to generous hospitality, and a feast for the senses. Imagine a centerpiece dish so magnificent, so aromatic, and so utterly delicious that it commands attention and admiration. This isn't your everyday dinner; this is a culinary journey into the heart of tradition, where succulent lamb, infused with exotic spices, is slow-roasted to fall-off-the-bone perfection and typically served alongside a rich, fragrant rice pilaf studded with nuts and often peas. Preparing a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi might seem daunting, but with this comprehensive guide, you'll be well on your way to mastering this iconic Middle Eastern dinner recipe, bringing a taste of authentic luxury to your own table.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozzy" or "Ouzy," is a grand Middle Eastern dish renowned for its spectacular presentation and incredible flavor. While the name "Ouzi" can sometimes refer to smaller individual pastries or pockets filled with spiced rice and meat, the version we're exploring here is the show-stopping whole slow-roasted lamb. At its core, it features a whole leg or shoulder of lamb, meticulously marinated with a blend of aromatic spices, then slow-cooked until it reaches an unparalleled tenderness. The magic of Lamb Ouzi truly unfolds when this melt-in-your-mouth lamb is served atop a bed of fragrant basmati rice, which itself is a masterpiece of flavor – often sautéed with ground meat, toasted nuts like almonds and pine nuts, and green peas, all seasoned with a symphony of spices such as allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, and black pepper. This dish is a staple at weddings, Eid celebrations, and large family gatherings, symbolizing abundance and warmth.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create this magnificent feast, careful selection of fresh, quality ingredients is key.

**For the Whole Slow Roasted Lamb:**
*   1 whole bone-in leg of lamb (approx. 6-8 lbs / 2.7-3.6 kg) or boneless lamb shoulder
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   8-10 cloves garlic, minced
*   Juice of 1 lemon
*   2 tablespoons ground cumin
*   2 tablespoons ground coriander
*   1 tablespoon sweet paprika
*   1 tablespoon allspice
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1 teaspoon ground black pepper
*   2 tablespoons sea salt
*   1 cup chicken or vegetable broth (for the roasting pan)
*   Optional: Fresh rosemary or thyme sprigs

**For the Spiced Rice Pilaf (Ouzi Rice):**
*   3 cups basmati rice, rinsed thoroughly
*   1/4 cup butter or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 lb ground lamb or beef (optional, but highly recommended for flavor)
*   1/2 cup slivered almonds, toasted
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1 cup frozen peas
*   2 teaspoons allspice
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1 teaspoon ground black pepper
*   1 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   5 cups chicken or vegetable broth

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh parsley, chopped
*   Extra toasted slivered almonds and pine nuts

## How to Make Lamb Ouzi: Step-by-Step Instructions

Embark on this culinary journey with patience and precision, and you'll be rewarded with an unforgettable dish.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the leg of lamb dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty side of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, allspice, cinnamon, black pepper, and sea salt to form a thick paste. Rub this marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. For best results, cover the lamb and refrigerate it overnight (or at least 4 hours) to allow the flavors to penetrate.
2.  **Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. Pour the 1 cup of broth into the bottom of the pan and add rosemary or thyme sprigs if using. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil. Roast for 4-5 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C) for medium-rare, or 160°F (71°C) for medium. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up slightly. The lamb should be incredibly tender, almost falling off the bone.
3.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This step is crucial for juicy, tender meat, allowing the juices to redistribute.
4.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice Pilaf:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the Ouzi rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter or ghee over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. If using ground lamb/beef, add it now and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
5.  **Cook the Rice:** Add the rinsed basmati rice, allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper, and salt to the pot. Stir well to coat the rice and spices, toasting lightly for 2-3 minutes. Pour in the 5 cups of chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
6.  **Finish the Rice:** Once the rice is cooked, remove it from the heat and let it sit, covered, for another 5 minutes. Gently fluff the rice with a fork. Stir in the toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and frozen peas.
7.  **Assemble and Serve:** Carve the slow-roasted lamb into generous portions or present it whole on a magnificent serving platter. Arrange the fragrant spiced rice around or beneath the lamb. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and extra toasted nuts.

## Pro Tips for the Best Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving the perfect Lamb Ouzi involves a few key techniques that can elevate your dish from good to unforgettable.

*   **Marination Time is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. Allowing the lamb to marinate overnight (12-24 hours) ensures the spices penetrate deeply, resulting in a more flavorful and tender roast.
*   **Low and Slow Roasting:** The "slow roasted" aspect isn't just a suggestion; it's essential. A low oven temperature (300°F / 150°C) over several hours breaks down the tough connective tissues in the lamb, yielding incredibly tender, juicy meat that practically melts in your mouth. Higher temperatures will dry out the lamb.
*   **Basting for Moisture:** Although covered, occasionally basting the lamb with its own pan juices during the roasting process can help keep it moist and infuse more flavor.
*   **Resting the Meat:** This step is non-negotiable. Resting allows the meat fibers to relax and reabsorb the juices, ensuring a tender and succulent result. Cutting into the lamb too soon will cause the juices to run out, leaving you with drier meat.
*   **Perfect Rice Texture:** Rinse your basmati rice thoroughly until the water runs clear to remove excess starch, which prevents stickiness. Toasting the nuts separately and adding them at the end preserves their crunch and flavor. Don't overcook the rice; it should be fluffy, not mushy.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a complete meal in itself, but traditional accompaniments enhance the dining experience and provide a refreshing contrast to the rich flavors.

*   **Fresh Salads:** A crisp Fattoush salad (with toasted pita, mixed greens, and a tangy sumac dressing) or a vibrant Tabbouleh (parsley, tomato, bulgur) offers a fresh counterpoint.
*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple yogurt sauce, perhaps with grated cucumber, garlic, and fresh mint (similar to a tzatziki), provides a cooling element.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles, such as pickled turnips or cucumbers, add a delightful sour crunch.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Perfect for scooping up any extra rice or meat juices.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Lamb Ouzi is magnificent, feel free to adapt it to your preferences or what you have on hand.

*   **Lamb Cut:** If a whole leg is too large, a bone-in lamb shoulder can be used, requiring similar slow-roasting times. For smaller gatherings, even lamb shanks can be prepared with the same marinade and served with the Ouzi rice.
*   **Rice Add-ins:** Get creative with the rice! Dried fruits like apricots or raisins can add a touch of sweetness. Different vegetables such as finely diced carrots or corn kernels can also be incorporated.
*   **Spice Profile:** Adjust the spices to your liking. A touch of dried rose petals can add a subtle floral note, while a pinch of chili flakes can introduce a gentle heat.
*   **Vegetarian Ouzi Rice:** For guests who don't eat meat, the Ouzi rice can be made entirely vegetarian by omitting the ground lamb/beef and using vegetable broth. It's still incredibly flavorful on its own.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Lamb Ouzi

**Can I prepare Lamb Ouzi ahead of time?**
You can definitely do some prep work in advance. The lamb can be marinated up to 2 days ahead of time. The Ouzi rice can also be made a day in advance and gently reheated on the stovetop with a splash of broth. The lamb can also be slow-roasted a day ahead, cooled, and then gently reheated in a low oven, covered, until warmed through.

**What's the best cut of lamb for Ouzi?**
A bone-in leg of lamb or lamb shoulder is ideal for whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi. The bone adds flavor and helps the meat stay moist. These cuts are best for long, slow cooking, which results in maximum tenderness.

**How do I store leftovers?**
Store leftover lamb and rice separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently in the microwave or on the stovetop, adding a little broth or water to the rice to prevent it from drying out.

**Is Lamb Ouzi spicy?**
Traditionally, Lamb Ouzi is not spicy in the sense of chili heat. Its flavor profile is aromatic and warm, derived from spices like allspice, cinnamon, and cumin. However, you can always add a pinch of cayenne pepper or chili flakes to the marinade or rice if you prefer a spicier kick.

**Can I cook it faster?**
While you technically *can* cook lamb at a higher temperature for a shorter time, it will not achieve the same fall-off-the-bone tenderness and succulence that slow roasting provides. For the authentic Lamb Ouzi experience, patience is truly a virtue.

Bringing the tradition and splendor of Middle Eastern cuisine to your kitchen, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is a dish that promises to impress and delight. It’s a labor of love, but every moment spent preparing this magnificent feast is rewarded with an unforgettable dining experience. Gather your loved ones, set a grand table, and enjoy the rich aromas and exquisite flavors of this truly special Middle Eastern dinner recipe.
